Abstract The aim of this research is to study the effect of magnetic field on the growth of the bacterial culture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the custom-synthesised superparamagnetic iron oxide (SPION) nanoparticles have adequate physicochemical properties for potential use as delivery systems in magnetofection, and their cellular uptake and trafficking into cells is dependent on cell type and the presence of an external magnetic field.
the prepared SPIONs are biocompatible and have potential for magnetofection.
SPIONs are a potential tool for magnetofection, and their uptake is significantly increased by an external magnetic field, especially in malignant cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of an external magnetic field can significantly increase the uptake of SPION nanoparticles into cells, which may be beneficial for magnetofection.
the prepared SPIONs have potential as a delivery system for magnetofection.
